steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Line a baking sheet with aluminum foil; lightly coat with cooking spray.
Lay puff pastry on the prepared baking sheet; center Brie wheel on pastry sheet. Evenly spread jam over top of Brie; sprinkle walnuts on top jam. Fold puff pastry over top of Brie; seal completely.
Bake in the preheated oven until pastry is golden brown, about 20 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Raspberry Walnut Baked Brie
raw_recipe.description: This four-ingredient recipe for raspberry walnut baked brie combines puffed pastry, Brie cheese, raspberry jam, and walnuts for an impressive appetizer.
raw_recipe.name: Raspberry Walnut Baked Brie

review.reviewBody: Try splitting a small brie in 1/2 horizontally (a wire works well) & put the jam & walnuts inside. Then wrap with phyllo, puff pastry or crescent roll dough. This makes a spectacular presentation & its own "bread" to eat it with. bake @ 350 about 30 - 35 min.

4 people nearly ate the whole thing before dinner! I didn't expect this to be the 'hit' of the dinner, but it dominated much of the conversation. Before baking I did drizzle some real maple syrup and brown sugar on top to brown it. Very good.

I made these for a pot luck and they were almost all gone as soon as the plate was on the table! I made a few adjustments to the recipe.
Firstly, I made them with phyllo dough in mini-muffin trays. I cut the phyllo into triangles and brushed them lightly with olive oil. It took six triangle per mini-muffin spot. I then put a chuck of brie, a LITTLE bit of jam I had made testers before and too much Jam overpowered the brie and added walnuts on top. 

I fold the edges of the phyllo over top. THey look SO GOOD and the Phyllo dough made it a little fancier looking! 

I brought them there cold then heated them in the oven on 350 for about 5 minutes... let cool about 5 minutes before serving them you are done!

GREAT RECIPE!

this is also great with won ton wrappers. spray muffin tins, line with the wrapper, bake 350 12-15 min. place a wedge of brie in cup, top with jam (good with cranberry relish too)return to oven covered lightly with a piece of foil and bake for another 5 min. Enjoy! Lizzy

I would make this again. It was delicious. I used frozen raspberries, as I did not have jam. I mashed the raspberries with my mortar and pestal, spread on the cheese topped with the chopped walnuts. Delicious!!

I have made this gorgeous, easy, and show-stoppingly delicious baked brie at least a dozen times, and (almost) every time it is such a hit! I make it exactly as written except I do what someone suggested and slice the brie carefully with a sharp knife width-wise and put the jam and nuts inside, like a sandwich, then wrap the puff pastry so it's flat on the top. Sometimes I make leaves out of bits of pastry to decorate it on top. Note: I use Pepperidge Farms puff pastry for great results. One time I used phyllo dough and it turned out too chewy and almost 'chalky,' so I stick with P.Farms. THANK YOU, Laura, for sharing this great recipe!

This is such a great recipe. I did split it horizontly, and put in finely sliced apples, chopped walnuts and raspberry jam. (seedless) brushed the outside of the pastry w/ egg white, and.....for a bit of sweetness.........melted about 3 tablespoons of butter and a touch of cinnimon, and burshed that over the egg white!! YUM!! Making it tomorow for Super Bowl Sunday! Go Colts!!

This is soo yummy!!! Very easy to make,was a big hit for our family gathering Christmas eve.Used a wedge, couldn't find a round brie, took the rind off top, spread the raspberry jam & walnuts on the brie itself, so it could melt with the brie, made it so much nicer to eat!!

Couldn't find a round brie, so bought an 8 oz wedge of brie. spread the jam and the walnuts on the puff pastry before placing the brie on the pastry. Wrapped it up best as I can and it took a while for the top to turn golden but it did and tastes great with crackers!
This was a great hit and my house. The only thing I added was brushing the top of the pastry with egg so it made that crispy flaky top.

I took the suggestion of others and made it with mini phyllo (aka fillo) cups instead. Great idea! Everybody loved them. This is a recipe I'll definitely be making many more times. It's so quick and easy. Loved it!
Tasted good but way too greasy!! Will not make again.
I loved it! It certainly was a different dish from a boring cheese & fruit appetizer and the nuts are a good touch. Will make again.
I’ve made this several times with toasted almonds and raspberry jam but I like to use the jam with the seeds. Most of the recipes here call for seedless and I was wondering why?
Really good. I served with ginger snaps. I baked for 20 minutes but could have added another 5. Crust was soft but it was still delicious.
Does not taste good.
I used pepper jelly (cranberry pepper jelly is even better!) I have also made this with my homemade apricot jam, too. I usually omit the nuts. Yum, yum!
Great recipe-- I used slivered almonds instead of walnuts because I prefer the texture. It was a big hit at the office christmas party
Loved it - was a huge hit at my holiday party
So easy, so delicious. Cheese, nuts, sweet berry preserves, what could be wrong with that combination?!?
